  5131	## D-083: The additive effective-clearable-effect expression is a disclosure obligation, not an acceptance threshold
  5132	
  5133	- Date: 2026-07-29
  5134	- Status: accepted (magistrate-adjudicated from primary text on a referred
  5135	  Sol-vs-Opus split; review finding B3 → NOT-A-DEFECT; no code change)
  5136	- Applies to: `joulewise/analysis_engine/claims.py`, every artifact or prose
  5137	  surface that publishes an attribution-limited floor
  5138	- Supersedes nothing; clarifies the enforcement semantics of D-078 clause 11
  5139	
  5140	`effective_clearable_effect = floor_j + claim_side_bound_j` is a statement
  5141	the project owes its readers, **not** a gate a claim must clear. The
  5142	**two-gate structure** in `claims.py:324-363` — the floor gate containing the
  5143	anchor term, and each claim's decision interval separately consuming the
  5144	member's `E_clock_anchor_shift_bound_j` — is the **ratified design**.
  5145	
  5146	Grounds (primary text read directly this session, not packet-trusted):
  5147	
  5148	1. **D-078 clause 11's own words.** It introduces the additive expression as a
  5149	   *consequence* of the two-object design it has just ratified: "These are
  5150	   different objects … and both are legitimate, but the **consequence** is
  5151	   that the effective clearable effect is FLOOR + CLAIM-SIDE BOUND … Every
  5152	   artifact publishing an attribution-limited floor must **state this
  5153	   explicitly** so that neither term is later removed as an apparent double
  5154	   count." The operative verb is *state*. Science requires the disclosure;
  5155	   the code already enforces it (`claims.py:274-304`, exact-equality
  5156	   validation else `floor_artifact_invalid`).
  5157	2. **D-079 clause 5.** "The attribution-width floor is a diagnostic; the
  5158	   **operative floor is the claim gate**." The gate is the floor — not floor
  5159	   plus bound.
  5160	3. **The referral question — do the two citations address different objects?
  5161	   YES, explicitly.** D-082 clause 2 / contract rule 8 ("NEVER sum
  5162	   allowances") governs FLOOR-SIDE component composition (absolute vs
  5163	   comparative allowances *inside* the gate). D-078 clause 11's claim-side
  5164	   bound is consumed by the claim's decision interval — a different object,
  5165	   per clause 11's own words. The D-082 citation is therefore **orthogonal**
  5166	   to B3 and neither compels nor forbids the reading; the D-078-internal
  5167	   consequence/disclosure reading is decisive on its own and D-079 clause 5
  5168	   corroborates it.
  5169	4. **Consistency.** An additive *acceptance* gate would require its own
  5170	   ratification — it would sit in tension with D-082 clause 2's direction of
  5171	   travel as merged.
  5172	
  5173	**Dissent preserved (Sol, xhigh review lens):** that the ratified text makes
  5174	the sum the operative bar ("not the floor alone"), worked through an executed
  5175	example (a claim of 8.63 J admitted against floor 3.59 plus a comparable
  5176	claim-side bound). The magistrate finds the ratified text does not support it:
  5177	that phrase is the same sentence's honest description of what a claim must in
  5178	practice clear across BOTH gates jointly, and does not convert the disclosure
  5179	into a single summed gate. `claims.py` was untouched by the mint series, so
  5180	the disposition carries no merge impact either way.
  5181	
  5182	The practical phrasing already circulating in project notes — "effective bar
  5183	= floor + claim-side ≈ 5 J for phase contrasts" — **stays**, as the correct
  5184	description of what a claim must clear across both gates jointly. This entry
  5185	governs the *enforcement* semantics only.
  5186	
  5187	Revisit when: someone proposes a single summed acceptance gate (which would
  5188	need its own ratification), or a floor artifact is published without the
  5189	clause-11 disclosure.
  5190

  7363	## D-114: T3-CHAIN DESCOPE — t3 stays the interactive control plane; t3-resident-during-measurement-windows is DROPPED (Ed directive, supersedes the 2026-08-03 T3-DRIVE priority)
  7364	
  7365	**Date:** 2026-08-05 (Ed, in-thread, during the desk session).
  7366	**Status:** RATIFIED by the directive's own author. This reverses Ed's
  7367	2026-08-03 ~23:55 T3-DRIVE-PRIORITY directive. Under rule 11 a
  7368	lieutenant may not self-exempt from a standing priority; that
  7369	constraint does not bind Ed reversing his own instruction, so no cold
  7370	gate was convened. The lead proposed the descope shape; Ed ruled.
  7371	
  7372	**Question.** The t3-drive chain (host-wide quiet lease, refuse-at-arm,
  7373	resident watcher, t3 handoff/relaunch, README banner projection, plus
  7374	an app-up/app-down characterization pair to decide app-adjacent window
  7375	admissibility) had grown a root-owned, sudo-capable, credential-bearing
  7376	surface — a 7-blocker focused audit on commit 1 alone, and a design
  7377	consult showing the credential could not be honestly removed without
  7378	also revising Q10/Q11/Q13/Q19/Q24 as a set. Ed: "is the juice worth the
  7379	squeeze for a UX improvement of using t3 as a control plane?" and "I am
  7380	tired of wasting time on this control plane stuff and want to get back
  7381	to the project."
  7382	
  7383	**Ruling.**
  7384	1. **KEEP — t3 as the INTERACTIVE control plane.** Ed drives sessions
  7385	   from t3, including remotely and away from the measurement machine.
  7386	   This costs nothing and requires no guard machinery.
  7387	2. **DROP — t3 resident during measurement windows.** Claim windows
  7388	   return to the proven path: quit t3, ordinary guarded shell, zero
  7389	   agent sessions, fresh §5A, walk away. Every successful claim window
  7390	   to date used exactly this path. The app-up admissibility question is
  7391	   therefore MOOT, not answered.
  7392	3. **QUIET-GUARD-01 re-scoped to COMMIT 1 ONLY** — the host-wide quiet
  7393	   lease and process census, installed-INACTIVE. Retained on non-t3
  7394	   merit: it gives the ordinary guarded-shell launcher a MECHANICAL
  7395	   refuse-at-arm census, replacing today's procedural eyeballing. Its
  7396	   seven audit blockers are still fixed to the safety bar before it
  7397	   lands (it is root-adjacent regardless of who calls it).
  7398	4. **SHELVED:** QUIET-GUARD commits 2-4 (launcher interception, t3
  7399	   handoff + resident watcher, t3-relaunch + banner projection + all
  7400	   credential handling); T3-CHAR-PAIR-01 (BOTH arms — the r03 re-capture
  7401	   and the app-DOWN arm); WO-T3-VIS-01; SEC5A-REMOTE-01 (its
  7402	   programmatic substrate lived in the dropped scope).
  7403	5. **T3-DRIVE-PRIORITY gate LIFTED** (`active_global_gates: []`); the
  7404	   project queue is ungated. The two in-flight t3-adjacent desk items
  7405	   (T3-AMEND-01 doctrine bookkeeping, COLDGATE-VALIDATOR-01) finish
  7406	   because both are cheap, near-complete, and independently useful.
  7407	6. **Q13's degraded tail is ACCEPTED as an edge case** (Ed, explicit):
  7408	   if a relaunch fails and no session returns, there is no remote
  7409	   signal. A failed relaunch requires physical presence anyway, so
  7410	   local discovery at next login is sufficient. This retires the
  7411	   requirement that motivated the unattended-push credential.
  7412	7. **Q10 (guard git identity WITH unattended push) is SUPERSEDED** —
  7413	   moot under the descope; no credential enters any guard path.
  7414	
  7415	**Design record preserved for any future revival** (from the 2026-08-05
  7416	credential consult, before the descope was ruled): a credentialed
  7417	network pusher running DURING a quiet window contradicts the window's
  7418	defining property. The correct shape is credentials only at the
  7419	unprivileged interactive boundary (pre-arm and post-window pushes), a
  7420	PRE-ARMED SERVER-SIDE DEAD-MAN ALARM for the no-return case (which also
  7421	catches total host death), a dedicated non-login service UID rather
  7422	than HOME-restore env scrubbing (root is otherwise ambiently
  7423	credential-reachable via git helpers / SSH / Keychain), and a banner
  7424	that can only truthfully say ARMING_REQUESTED pre-window.
  7425	
  7426	**Consequences.** The successor's queue is the science queue: the two

  3208	
  3209	## D-061: Review-layer evaluation rule v2 (replaces the two-zero-sessions drop rule)
  3210	
  3211	- Date: 2026-07-09
  3212	- Status: accepted (C-027; process-layer, within council authority)
  3213	- Phase: cross-phase / process instrumentation
  3214	
  3215	Context: the "drop a layer after two zero-catch sessions" rule was
  3216	falsified by its own record — integration review returned zero unique
  3217	catches twice (C-017, CP-5) and then caught five real cross-stream seams
  3218	(C-024). Mechanical application would have deleted the layer immediately
  3219	before its highest-value session.
  3220	
  3221	Decision: layer evaluation uses (a) applicability decided by
  3222	PRE-DECLARED mechanical predicates (e.g. integration review counts only
  3223	when 2+ independently developed streams merge touching a shared
  3224	contract/consumer/generated artifact), never post-hoc judgment; (b) an
  3225	outcome taxonomy separating accepted-unique-defect / duplicate /
  3226	clean-verification / false-positive-suppression — suppression is
  3227	valuable but is not a catch; (c) fixed severity weights declared before
  3228	the session; (d) three applicable exposures TRIGGER an expected-loss
  3229	review decision, never automatic deletion; (e) safety, final-head, and
  3230	integration layers are never auto-dropped on zero-defect streaks —
  3231	they are judged by expected-loss reduction.
  3232	
  3233	Alternatives considered: keep the two-zero rule (falsified); "three
  3234	applicable sessions, severity-weighted" as free-text judgment (rejected
  3235	in council — reintroduces the discretion that made the old rule
  3236	unfalsifiable).
  3237	
  3238	## D-062: Confirmatory sampling policy — fixed n, explicit demotion, no silent top-ups

class="source-file">docs/<wbr>council_log.md</span><span class="source-commit">commit 1af9f92</span></span></div> <!-- rendered: marked@18.0.6 --> <h1>Council Log</h1> <p>Chronicle of multi-model review councils: sessions where more than one model reviews, counterreviews, or votes on JouleWise work before it lands. Companion to <code>docs/decision_log.md</code> (which records WHAT was decided about the system; this file records HOW cross-model review reached it). One entry per council session; keep entries concise — positions, votes, resolutions, and follow-ups, not transcripts.</p> <p>Standing council roles (adopted C-001; process decision D-031):</p> <ul> <li><strong>Claude (lead/orchestrator)</strong> — scopes work, diagnoses live/hardware failures, runs adversarial review workflows, owns bookkeeping and the final merge decision, and is the only member that touches real hardware.</li> <li><strong>Codex / gpt-5.5 (peer implementer-reviewer)</strong> — implements against pinned specs, counterreviews findings on its own code, reverse-reviews Claude&#39;s commits and orchestration decisions, and is asked for design judgment explicitly (&quot;argue the tradeoffs before you code&quot;).</li> <li><strong>Opus subagents (fast reviewers)</strong> — parallel lower-level sweeps (commit hygiene, docs consistency, fixture audits) whose findings feed the discussion; cheap enough to run every session.</li> </ul> <p>(Amended 2026-07-08: the Opus fast-reviewer tier was dropped at C-006 after zero unique catches; lead-driven pipelines are the default per C-010; Ed granted standing self-merge-with-review authority in the C-010 addendum.)</p> <p>Disagreements are discussed in at most one or two rounds; unresolved disagreements are decided by the lead and recorded here with the dissent.
